To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

strontium chloride is a suitable marker for intestinal calcium bioavailability and that a simple test variable (the fractional absorption at 4 h after oral intake) has been selected to represent absolute bioavailability.

the fractional absorption at the end of the absorption phase (240 min after intake) after oral intake of strontium is representative for absolute bioavailable calcium, that the intraindividual variability of this parameter is similar to that of calcium absorption tests based on calcium isotopes, that the in vitro bioavailability of stronium is similar to that for calcium and that strontium absorption is not influenced by the calcium intake.
the absolute bioavailability (A) of strontium is a suitable test variable for the assessment of the intestinal calcium absorption (I) in man.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of a simple clinical absorption test for calcium.
the validation of a test variable that may be used as a measure of the absolute bio-availability of calcium and its modulation.
the validation of a simple, reliable and reproducible test for the assessment of calcium absorption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fc240 of orally administered SrCl2 can be used in a simple clinical test as a measure of true calcium absorption.
the test for intestinal calcium absorption is valid, but that the test variable is not.
the test is not yet ready for clinical use, but the data are promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strontium is a good marker to measure the intestinal calcium absorption in humans.
the Fc240 is representative of absolute bioavailabilty and that this test variable is a simple test for intestinal calcium absorption.

the Fc240 is the best test variable for the absolute bioavailable fraction of orally administered strontium, and the Fc240 can be used as a measure of absolute intestinal calcium absorption and as a test of the modulation of this absorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to show that strontium can be used as a surrogate for calcium in terms of intestinal absorption, and that we were able for the first time to show that the fractional absorption of strontium at 4 hours is a good surrogate of the true absorption of calcium.
the Fc240 is a good test variable for the measurement of intestinal calcium absorption.
strontium is a good candidate for the study of calcium metabolism.
